fact: The Star reports that Kenya enacted the Access to Information Act, 2016, giving effect to Article 35 of the Constitution, and that a forum assessed its implementation by public institutions.
The Star reports that the 2023 Access to Information Regulations, made under the Act, define proactive disclosure and set what public entities must publish.

The Daily Nation reports that the Access to Information Act guarantees the right to information under Article 35 of the Constitution; the document gives no year for it, so the date is the article's publication date.

The Commission on Administrative Justice (Ombudsman) says it will engage 54 public institutions to strengthen compliance with the Access to Information (ATI) Act, 2016, and says many institutions do not routinely publish information the Act requires.
